stdout_tail:
Both files are in place and match the required structure.

**Finding:** Model family has a real, statistically meaningful effect on predictive performance for this dataset, though the practical magnitude is modest. Comparing Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (HistGradientBoostingClassifier), and k-NN via 5-fold CV ROC-AUC:

| Model | CV ROC-AUC |
|---|---|
| Gradient Boosting | 0.927 |
| Logistic Regression | 0.906 |
| Random Forest | 0.903 |
| k-NN | 0.895 |

The spread across families (0.033) is about 10.7x larger than typical fold-to-fold noise (0.003), so the differences aren't just sampling variance — Gradient Boosting reliably wins. That said, even the weakest model (k-NN, 0.895) isn't far behind, and plain logistic regression is nearly as good as Random Forest, suggesting the underlying relationships are largely captured by linear/additive structure — model choice matters, but preprocessing/features do a lot of the work already.

Code (`analysis.py`) and results (`result.json`) are saved in the working directory.

parsed_result.summary: Model family has a real but modest effect on predictive performance: 5-fold CV ROC-AUC ranges from 0.895 (kNN) to 0.927 (GradientBoosting), a spread of 0.032 that is roughly 10.7x larger than typical fold-to-fold noise (0.003). Boosted/bagged tree ensembles outperform k-NN and logistic regression, but even the weakest model (logistic regression) is competitive, indicating the features are largely linearly separable and model choice matters less than good preprocessing.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: CV ROC-AUC range across model families (max - min)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: One-hot encoding for all categorical features (same representation across all models, so comparison isolates model family rather than feature engineering); missing values in workclass/occupation/native-country kept as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than imputed or dropped; numeric features standardized; single stratified 75/25 train/test split with 5-fold stratified CV on the training set for variance estimation; 4 model families compared (Logistic Regression, Random Forest with 300 trees, HistGradientBoosting, k-NN with k=25); primary metric ROC-AUC (threshold-independent, appropriate given ~24%/76% class imbalance) with accuracy as a secondary metric; hyperparameters left at reasonable defaults / lightly chosen (not tuned via grid search, so absolute numbers could shift a few points with tuning, though relative ranking is expected to be stable); random_state=42 throughout for reproducibility.
